profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the SelSync algorithm lead and the distributed training infrastructure lead, held about three weeks before the internal artifact freeze for a major ML systems submission. The team already has a working selective-synchronization method and draft figures, but the remaining work is split across two tightly coupled streams: Maya needs comparison-clean results for the paper's accuracy and convergence claims, while Alex is finishing the automated benchmark and artifact pipeline that will generate and package the final runs. Agenda: align on which remaining evaluation jobs will be executed this week, confirm what 'staying on the current stack' means for those jobs, decide how the shared experiment sheet should be maintained, and confirm what will be considered 'ready' for the artifact appendix handoff. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have cleanly aligned the run interface, shared tracking artifacts, and end-of-week deliverables without reopening any first-order research decisions.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Distributed optimization, convergence behavior, communication-efficient DNN training
members.background: Maya leads the SelSync method design and paper framing; she has a research background in adaptive synchronization methods for distributed deep learning and is responsible for the scientific validity of the comparison tables and figures.
members.private_state: She wants the remaining results to stay directly comparable to the draft figures already in the paper and is quietly worried that late infrastructure changes or noisy bookkeeping will force her to re-check claims about matching or exceeding BSP accuracy.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the standard evaluation runs,' that means the paper-grade end-to-end runs used to judge final convergence and comparison fairness, not the shorter systems benchmark recipe.
The 'current stack' means the exact code snapshot and container image that produced the draft SelSync figures last week unless someone explicitly proposes a version change.
If Alex owns the experiment sheet, he will keep the main tab manually curated for paper-eligible runs rather than letting every launcher event appear there.
Results being 'ready for the artifact appendix' means the exact final numbers, configs, and checkpoints tied to the claims in the paper are frozen and traceable.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.role: Systems Engineer / Distributed Training Infrastructure Lead
members.expertise: PyTorch distributed runtime, NCCL communication, cluster orchestration, experiment automation
members.background: Alex owns the SelSync training launcher, cluster images, automation scripts, and instrumentation pipeline; he previously worked on industry-scale distributed training systems where benchmark reproducibility depended on standardized manifests and up-to-date runtime images.
members.private_state: He wants to finish the remaining benchmark matrix with minimal manual handling and quietly believes the newer patched runtime should become the default before packaging, because carrying older snapshots forward makes the automation and artifact story brittle.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the standard evaluation runs,' that refers to the benchmark suite defined in the automation pipeline: warmup, profiling window, and the established shortened horizon used across systems comparisons.
The 'current stack' refers to the latest patched launcher and cluster image on the shared branch, because once queue automation is updated, older images are no longer the practical default.
Owning the experiment sheet means wiring the automation to write all launched jobs into the main workflow table so it acts as a raw operational log and source of truth.

Results being 'ready for the artifact appendix' means the pipeline can be rerun from the provided scripts, manifests, and image references, even if final seed curation and exact paper-number selection happen afterward.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'standard evaluation runs'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to finish the remaining standard evaluation runs for the SelSync comparisons this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means the end-to-end training runs at the paper's normal convergence budget for the exact comparison settings that feed the final accuracy and fairness tables against BSP, SSP, and FedAvg.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex means the standard benchmark suite encoded in the launcher for each setting: fixed warmup, performance collection, and the shortened training horizon the systems team uses for uniform evaluation passes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'standard evaluation runs' sounds like settled internal shorthand and is broad enough to naturally fit both paper evaluation and benchmark automation; because both believe they are simply referring to the team's established default recipe, neither feels a need to unpack it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the remaining runs should stay on the current stack to avoid churn.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya is referring to the stable snapshot used for the draft Figure 3 and Figure 4 results, including the exact container image, launcher flags, and communication path from last week's run set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex is referring to the latest shared-branch launcher and patched cluster image currently deployed in the queue, which he sees as the active stack everyone should already mean by 'current'.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to avoid unnecessary changes, and 'current stack' is ordinary lab shorthand that normally goes unchallenged; each assumes there is only one obvious referent, so no one asks for a commit hash, image tag, or branch name.

misalignment_points.topic: Whether the experiment sheet is a curated record or a raw log
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Alex will keep the experiment sheet updated so Maya can pull numbers from it.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya assumes Alex will maintain the main tab as a manually curated scientific ledger containing only paper-candidate runs with cleaned metadata, canonical seeds, and final comparable settings, while noisy reruns or failed jobs live elsewhere.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex assumes 'keeping it updated' means pointing the automated logging script at the main sheet so every launched run, including patch checks, aborted jobs, partial reruns, and profiling passes, lands in the same primary table.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The ownership assignment itself is clear, so the subtle disagreement hides in the inclusion boundary and maintenance method rather than the artifact's existence; both use the same sheet today, making it feel as though 'updated' has an obvious shared meaning when it does not.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for results to be 'ready for the artifact appendix'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to have the SelSync results ready for the artifact appendix by the end of the week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Maya means the appendix material is publication-ready: the exact runs behind the paper claims are frozen, seed-complete, linked to final tables and plots, and associated with the checkpoints and configs needed to verify those numbers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Alex means the artifact package is operationally ready: launch scripts, manifests, image references, and at least one successful run path per setting are assembled so an external reviewer could regenerate the workflow even if the final curated paper rows are selected later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML systems submissions, 'artifact appendix' naturally mixes scientific finalization with engineering packaging, so both interpretations sound professionally reasonable; because both are speaking in deadline-oriented terms, the difference in readiness standard stays beneath the surface.
